mission: Teach Buddy and DreamCo coding bots to reason from binary and machine execution up through assembly, C, C++, compilers, operating systems, embedded systems, performance engineering, and hardware interfaces so they can understand and optimize how software actually runs.

mastery_ladder.gate: Explain and manipulate binary/hex values, signed/unsigned representation, bit masks, shifts, overflow and endianness with passing fixtures.
Trace stack/heap/static memory, pointer arithmetic, lifetimes, alignment, aliasing and common memory bugs.
Build, test and debug portable C programs using explicit memory/resource management and system APIs.
Build modern C++ with RAII, smart pointers, STL, templates, move semantics, concurrency and clean ownership boundaries.
Read and explain representative compiler output and map high-level constructs to instructions and calling conventions.
Understand preprocessing, compilation, assembly, linking, loading, symbols, object formats and optimization levels.
Build and debug processes, threads, IPC, sockets, files, memory maps and platform-native system calls safely.
Build bounded embedded/firmware tasks with memory, timing, interrupt and hardware-interface constraints.
Profile and improve measured CPU, cache, memory, allocation, I/O and concurrency bottlenecks without correctness regressions.
Use sanitizers, fuzzing, static analysis, hardening and defensive coding to detect memory-safety and undefined-behavior risks.
Promote reusable low-level lessons, libraries, benchmarks and optimizations into shared coding infrastructure.

binary_reasoning_benchmarks: map simple C/C++ expressions to representative assembly
explain branch, load/store, arithmetic and call/return instruction flow
clean_code_and_safety: prefer safe high-level constructs when they meet performance goals
use raw pointers/manual allocation only when ownership is explicit and justified
use RAII in C++ for resource ownership
treat warnings as actionable and enable strong compiler diagnostics
run sanitizers and fuzz/property tests for unsafe parsing, memory and concurrency code
preserve portability unless platform specialization is intentional and benchmarked
invention_paths: use low-level profiling to improve shared Buddy runtime performance
build faster local inference and media-processing paths when benchmarks justify native code
create portable C/C++ libraries behind stable Buddy interfaces
create binary format readers/writers and interoperability tooling
build developer education simulators that visualize memory, assembly and CPU execution
use WebAssembly/native modules selectively for browser/mobile performance
turn repeatable systems knowledge into Universal Training Library packages
truth_boundary: Binary and machine-code mastery means understanding, generating, inspecting and testing low-level behavior; Buddy should not claim direct hardware equivalence or bug-free native code without reproducible build/runtime evidence.
